recognize_zh: 鐵染色（Prussian blue）骨髓抹片中，多個紅血球母細胞的核周圍排列著一圈藍色鐵顆粒，環繞核周至少三分之一以上，即為環狀鐵粒母細胞（ring sideroblasts），是 MDS-RS 的診斷關鍵。
features: Multiple erythroblasts with coarse blue iron granules arranged in a perinuclear ring
Granules encircle one-third or more of the nuclear circumference (ring sideroblast definition)
Other erythroblasts with few scattered granules or none
Background myeloid cells with pink nuclear counterstain and no iron
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear stained with Prussian blue shows numerous erythroid precursors containing coarse blue iron granules arranged in a perinuclear ring encircling at least one-third of the nucleus, diagnostic of ring sideroblasts. Other erythroblasts contain few scattered siderotic granules, and myeloid cells are iron-negative. Ring sideroblasts should be enumerated as a percentage of erythroid precursors; ≥15% (or ≥5% with SF3B1 mutation) in the setting of cytopenia and exclusion of secondary causes supports myelodysplastic syndrome with ring sideroblasts.

ddx.dx: Alcohol, copper deficiency, zinc toxicity, or isoniazid
ddx.vs: These reversible secondary causes also produce ring sideroblasts; clinical history, copper/zinc levels, and resolution after removal of the cause distinguish them.
Inherited forms (ALAS2, SLC25A38) present early in life with microcytosis and lack a clonal myeloid mutation such as SF3B1.
Normal sideroblasts have a few fine granules scattered randomly in the cytoplasm rather than coarse granules in a perinuclear ring.
Ring sideroblasts are identical; MDS/MPN-RS-T is separated by thrombocytosis ≥450×10^9/L and ET-like megakaryocytes.
